517	## The data pipeline (`scraper/` and `data/`)
518	
519	The domain of this pack: getting show data out of edfringe.com and into the
520	committed files the site serves. Read it before touching `scraper/` or anything
521	under `data/`. The API's own field reference lives in
522	[scraper/SCRAPING.md](../../../../scraper/SCRAPING.md) and the file layout in
523	[scraper/README.md](../../../../scraper/README.md) — this is the working
524	judgment those two don't carry.
525	
526	### Verifying a scraper change against the live API
527	
528	Reaching `edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` is a live question — it was denied at the
529	CONNECT in 2026-08 and answered a server-side 403 on 2026-09-04 — so probe it (the `edfringe`
530	pack's egress section) rather than repeat either answer. Reaching the host is still not the
531	same as being able to drive it, so anything that must touch the API runs through a sanctioned
532	workflow: the `Scrape edfringe shows (full)` workflow
533	(`.github/workflows/scrape.yml`), `Fetch ticket prices (one-off)`
534	(`prices.yml`), or the `refresh-shows` / `refresh-tickets` scheduled tasks.
535	Never "verify" a scraper change by reasoning about what the API probably
536	returns — either have a sanctioned workflow run it, or say plainly that it is
537	unverified.
538	
539	For one-off API questions (a field's shape, an enum's value set, whether an
540	operation exists at all), `scraper/SCRAPING.md` is the reference. When it falls
541	short there is one legitimate source short of asking the owner:
542	**`www.edfringe.com` itself is reachable**, and its Next.js bundles carry the
543	client's complete GraphQL operation set — every query, mutation and fragment,
544	with full field selections. Recipe in SCRAPING.md ("Reaching it from a Claude
545	Code web session"). That is reading a public asset from an allowed host, and it
546	is how the "no bulk price endpoint" claim was finally settled. It tells you what
547	a query would look like, never what it returns — so a change checked only that
548	way is still unverified against live data and must be reported as such. If that
549	doesn't answer it either, ask the repo owner rather than building a bypass.
550	
551	`python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest` is the one transform check that runs
552	offline; it exercises raw→master→day-file→`shows.min.json` on a fixture, so a
553	normalizer change is verifiable here even though a fetch change is not. Because
554	it is the only offline verification a scraper change can get, it must stay wired
555	into `scripts/verify.sh` — the `edfringe-normalizer-selftest-in-verify` check
556	enforces that (a step *label* naming the self-test does not count; only a command
557	line does).
558	
559	### `ticketStatus`, never the `soldOut` boolean
560	
561	"Can I get a ticket" comes from the per-performance `ticketStatus`, not the
562	`soldOut` flag: a performance can be `soldOut: false` and still have nothing to
563	sell online (`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`). The site treats `SOLD_OUT` and
564	`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` as unavailable and everything else as available
565	(`NO_TICKETS_STATUSES` in `js/app.js`), and unknown means available. Any new
566	availability logic — client or scraper — keys off `ticketStatus`; `soldOut` is
567	carried through for display only.
568	
569	### A price belongs to a performance, not to a show
570	
571	The same run sells at several prices: previews cheaper than the main run,
572	weekends dearer than weekdays. The first price pass didn't know that — it
573	called `performancePrices` for **one** performance per show and filed the answer
574	under the show. Pre-festival the performance it picked was almost always the
575	earliest, i.e. a preview, so **1,016 of 3,664 priced shows (28%) published their
576	cheapest night as their price**: Alfie Brown's £15/£16 run shipped as £8.50.
577	
578	The fix is not a rule about previews, and adding a "skip previews" or
579	"price after date X" heuristic re-creates the same class of bug from a different
580	angle — it still picks one performance and hopes it represents the rest.
581	**Price every performance.** There is no bulk price *field*, but GraphQL aliases
582	make one request carry a whole show's run (`fetch_prices.prices_query`), so full
583	per-night pricing costs roughly the same ~3,700 requests as the old pass. There
584	is no call budget to economise against here, so don't design as if there were.
585	
586	Which payload gets which number is the load-bearing distinction:
587	
588	| payload | question it answers | price |
589	|---|---|---|
590	| `shows.min.json` (planner) | what does this *show* cost? | run-wide `priceMin`..`priceMax` |
591	| `data/days/*.json` (Now page) | what does it cost *tonight*? | that performance's own `pm` |
592	
593	A performance the cache has no entry for gets **no `pm` at all** — "Price TBC" —
594	rather than the show's minimum. Borrowing a neighbouring night's figure is
595	exactly the bug above, and a lower bound presented as the price is a lie about
596	money even when every number in it is real.
597	
598	### Prices are fetched once, and "unknown" is a third state the encoding must keep
599	
600	`data/prices.json` is a fetch-once cache (`scraper/fetch_prices.py`), off the
601	nightly path: a show's price bands are set when it goes on sale, unlike its
602	ticket status. `refresh-shows` reads the cache and carries the amounts through
603	untouched — it never re-fetches them. So the festival keeps adding shows the
604	cache has never seen, and **a show with no price is a normal, permanent state of
605	the data**, not a gap the pipeline should close.
606	
607	The cache carries two entry shapes and both must stay readable: current entries
608	have `sets` + `perfs` (per performance), and entries from the old pass have a
609	bare whole-show `min`/`max`. The migration completes one show per re-run, so
610	dropping the legacy shape — or emptying the cache to "start clean" — would blank
611	every price on the site until a full pass finished. `price_sets` reads both.
612	
613	Which means the encoding carries three states, not two, and every stage has to
614	preserve the distinction:
615	
616	| state | master | wire |
617	|---|---|---|
618	| costs nothing | `priceMin: 0` | `pm: 0` |
619	| priced | `priceMin: 22.5` | `pm: 22.5` |
620	| unknown | `priceMin: null` | no `pm` key at all |
621	
622	`priceMin: 0` and `free: true` are **not** the same claim and don't always agree.
623	The flag comes from the listing; the £0 can also come from the price API, which
624	returns a single `Price band 1` at £0.00 for a handful of shows the listing
625	doesn't flag free — pay-what-you-want, or a box office that never set a price
626	(10 of 3,664 in the first full run). Both readings are honest about what a ticket
627	costs, so the price path keys off `priceMin`, and `free` stays what the *listing*
628	said. Don't "fix" one to match the other.
629	
630	Never encode unknown as `0`, and never let a decoder default it to one: a stage
631	that collapses three states into two is lying about money, and nothing
632	downstream can recover the difference. What the site then *does* with an unknown
633	price is a product decision, not a pipeline one — it lives in `shared/price.js`.
634	
635	Two traps in the raw price payload, both already handled and both worth not
636	re-introducing: amounts arrive as **strings**, and nearly every show carries a
637	£0.00 "Personal Assistant" concession (a carer's companion ticket) that must not
638	be read as the cheapest price. See the pricing section of
639	[scraper/SCRAPING.md](../../../../scraper/SCRAPING.md).
640	
641	### The API stamps performances in UTC — cross the zone once, at the edge
642	
643	The listing API's `dateTime` is a real UTC instant (`"2026-08-06T11:45:00.000Z"`),
644	**not** Edinburgh wall-clock with a decorative `Z`. Slicing the digits out of that
645	string is the trap: it looks like it works — every date and time in it is
646	plausible — and in August it is silently an hour wrong for the whole catalogue.
647	That is exactly what shipped, and what #275 cost to undo: 60,115 performances
648	listed an hour early, with the tell being shows that name their own time (a 10am
649	"Shakespeare for Breakfast" sitting at 09:00).
650	
651	The pipeline has **one** time-zone crossing, and it is `normalize.local_date_start`.
652	`refresh_ticket_status.py` and `fetch_prices.py` share it so a performance is keyed
653	by the same local date and start everywhere. Everything written after it — the
654	master, `data/days/*.json`, `availability.min.json`, `shows.min.json` — is already
655	Edinburgh wall-clock, so **no stage downstream parses, converts, or re-offsets a
656	time**. Treating a stored value as UTC a second time is the same bug from the other
657	end.
658	
659	Two consequences to hold on to when touching this:
660	
661	- **A "now" compared against these times is read in Edinburgh too** — `js/clock.js`
662	  (`festivalNow` / `festivalDate`), never the device clock. A UK visitor cannot see
663	  the difference, which is why a device clock survives review; a visitor planning
664	  from another zone reintroduces the whole drift.
665	- **A conversion change is a full-snapshot change.** The committed data is generator
666	  output, so the fix is not complete until the master is rebuilt through the new
667	  conversion and every derived artifact regenerated from it. Shifting the boundary
668	  moves performances between day files (two late 31 Aug performances now fall into
669	  1 Sep, outside the August day files, and live only in the master and the planner's
670	  catalogue) — expect that and check it, rather than reading it as data loss.
671	
672	### Two client-cached files joined by key need a fingerprint, or a generation split breaks the join
673	
674	`shows.min.json` (catalogue) and `availability.min.json` (ticket-status
675	sidecar) are cached independently in the browser and joined client-side by
676	performance key (venue + date + time). The UTC time-shift fix (`c1bc2a6`,
677	above) moved every one of those keys by an hour — a browser still holding the
678	pre-fix sidecar cached alongside a post-fix catalogue joined at 6.2%
679	(3,751/60,115) instead of 100%, rendering every planner favourite "No dates."
680	even though both files were individually correct (#309). A per-file TTL has
681	no way to detect that two files it's serving came from incompatible backend
682	generations.
683	
684	The fix is `join_fingerprint(master)` in `scraper/normalize.py`, mirrored
685	exactly as `joinFingerprint()` in `plan/lib/hydrate.js` (same algorithm in
686	both languages — `normalize.py`'s self-test asserts they agree, and that a
687	moved start time changes the fingerprint while a price change doesn't),
688	carried as the sidecar's `k` field. `plan/plan.js` compares its own
689	`joinFingerprint()` of the catalogue it holds against the sidecar's `k` and
690	calls `evictCached()` on both URLs on a mismatch, forcing a refetch of the
691	matching pair. Any future backend change that moves a performance's join key
692	needs this same fingerprint-and-evict shape — a plain TTL bump doesn't cover
693	it, because both files can be individually "fresh enough" by TTL and still
694	belong to different generations.
695	
696	### The committed data is generated output — regenerate it, never hand-edit it
697	
698	`data/raw_pages/` is a git-ignored regenerable cache. `data/normalized/`,
699	`data/venues.json` and `data/days/` **are** committed, because the browser
700	fetches them — but they are still generator output. Fix the data by fixing
701	`scraper/normalize.py` and re-running it (`--merge` for a top-up, no flag for a
702	full rebuild from the raw cache); a hand-edit is silently overwritten by the next
703	`refresh-shows` run and leaves the bug in the generator.
704	
705	`data/prices.json` is the one exception, and it is an exception to the *direction*
706	rather than the rule: it is committed, but it is normalize.py's **input**, written
707	by `scraper/fetch_prices.py`. Nothing regenerates it on a schedule, so nothing
708	overwrites a hand-edit either — which is precisely why editing it by hand is still
709	wrong: the edit survives, silently disagreeing with the box office forever. Re-run
710	the fetch. The `edfringe-data-dir-is-generator-output` check allows it **by name**,
711	so a second file can't ride in on its shape.
712	
713	### A long-running workflow that commits generated data will race the hourly refresh
714	
715	Any workflow that writes to `data/normalized/`, `data/venues.json` or `data/days/`
716	and can run for more than about an hour is racing `refresh-tickets`, which pushes
717	to `main` every hour through the festival. A plain `git push` at the end of such a
718	run is not occasionally rejected — it is *guaranteed* to be, so the commit step has
719	to expect it. `#292` lost a full 2h39m price-fetch pass this way: the commit
720	existed only on the runner, and by the time it tried to push, `main` had moved.
721	
722	Recovery has to **re-derive, not merge** — every contested file is generator
723	output from both writers, so a rebase would conflict on generated bytes whose only
724	correct value is "whatever the generator says now," not either side's stored
725	version. `prices.yml`'s commit step (`.github/workflows/prices.yml`, the retry
726	loop in its "Commit prices and regenerated data" step) is the worked fix: on a
727	rejected push, fetch `origin/main`, take its generated files, regenerate from that
728	master plus this workflow's own non-generated input, retry. A new long-running
729	workflow that writes these paths needs the same shape from the start, not a
730	bespoke recovery discovered the same way after the fact.
731	
732	### Changing the wire format is a four-file change
733	
734	The day files and `shows.min.json` reference `data/venues.json`'s global lists
735	**by position** (`genre`, `room`, `subs`, `ts`; `g`, `rm`, `sg`, `ar`). That
736	encoding has one producer and two decoders, and they must move together:
737	
738	- producer — `scraper/normalize.py` (`build_lookups` / `build_day_files` /
739	  `minify_master` / `build_availability`)
740	- decoder 1 — `js/app.js` `adaptShow`, for the day files
741	- decoder 2 — `plan/lib/hydrate.js` `rehydrateShows`, the exact inverse of
742	  `minify_master`, round-tripped against the real committed files by
743	  `plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs`
744	
745	Add or drop an indexed field and all three change in the same commit. That the
746	indices still *resolve* is enforced by the `edfringe-lookup-indices` check — it
747	catches a lookup list regenerated without its day files, but nothing can catch a
748	decoder left reading the old key, so check both decoders by hand.
749	
750	Two properties of that encoding are load-bearing for caching, and both fail
751	silently:
752	
753	- **The lookup lists are append-only** (`extend_lookup`). The browser holds
754	  `shows.min.json` for four days and `venues.json` for one, so a stale catalogue
755	  is routinely decoded against a newer lookup file. An entry that changed index
756	  would relabel shows' genres and rooms with no error anywhere. Entries are never
757	  dropped, even once the master stops using them.
758	- **`shows.min.json` carries nothing that changes through the day.** Ticket
759	  status lives in `availability.min.json` (its own status list, indexing into
760	  nothing, so `refresh-tickets` can rewrite it alone). Putting a status back in
761	  the catalogue would tie that bulky download to the ticket refresh *and*
762	  freeze availability for anyone holding a cached copy — the bug in #249,
763	  re-created from the other end.
764	  `hydrate.test.mjs` asserts each wire performance carries only `d` and `s`.
765	
766	The same three-way move applies to plain (non-indexed) wire keys such as the
767	price fields `pm` / `px`, with one extra hazard: the round-trip test compares the
768	rehydrated record to the master **as JSON**, so a new master key has to appear in
769	the *same position* in `normalize_event`'s dict and in `rehydrateShows`'s object
770	literal. Adding it in one place and appending it in the other fails the
771	round-trip on key order alone, which reads as a data bug and isn't one.
772	
773	## The requirements harness
774	
775	How this repo runs its spec (`product/requirements.md`) as tests. The framework
776	conventions are the `executable-requirements` pack; the judgment layer is
777	`spec-driven-product` + the `writing-tests` skill. This pack carries only what
778	those don't: the mechanics of a **real-headless-browser** golden harness (the
779	canon's worked examples render with satori/jsdom or Flutter — this repo is the
780	first Playwright port) and the local approval/fixture policy. Layout, lanes and
781	commands live in [product/requirements/README.md](../../../../product/requirements/README.md)
782	— don't restate them; this file is the judgment and the traps.
783	
784	### The document reads as pictures
785	
786	- `product/requirements.md` is scanned by sight: under each visual leaf its
787	  golden is **visible, uncollapsed**; every textual expansion (acceptance
788	  notes, proof pointers) is **collapsed** in a `<details>` block. An optimal
789	  requirements document has almost no words on the page.
790	- **A visual leaf's statement is a line, not a paragraph.** The golden already
791	  carries the exact copy, counts, colours and placement — restating them in
792	  prose only competes with the picture. Say what is being asserted; let the
793	  image say how it looks. Anything genuinely not visible (a threshold, a rule
794	  behind the state, a condition that produced it) goes in a collapsed
795	  **Notes** block, never in the statement.
796	- **A golden is the smallest surface that proves its leaf** — an element crop,
797	  a clipped region, or a stitched composite (e.g. one grid lane narrowed to a
798	  few days, recomposed with its label and verdict columns, no header) — never
799	  the whole page or even the whole control. The capture recipe lives on the
800	  case (`capture: "<selector>"` or `capture(page, tools)`; see
801	  `shared/capture-tools.js`); whole-page capture is a deliberate exception,
802	  not a default. Scoping is judgment: crop to what the leaf asserts, keep just
803	  enough surroundings to orient.
804	- **A change over time is an animation, not a coded assertion.** When a
805	  requirement is about what an action *changes* — a dismissal that sticks, a
806	  pick that swaps one card for another — capture the same region before and
807	  after (and after a reload, where persistence is the point) and play the
808	  frames as one animated golden (`tools.animate`). A flow is shown as a flow.
809	  Reserve `stitchV`/`stitchH` for things that are genuinely side by side rather
810	  than sequential.
811	- **An animated golden is an APNG, never a GIF.** It animates in GitHub
812	  markdown exactly like a GIF. The encoder is `shared/png.js`'s
813	  `encodeAnimated`; the comparator detects an animated golden and compares
814	  bytes only, since a pixel differ reads one still frame and would describe
815	  the wrong thing.
816	
817	### A requirement is a feature, not a module
818	
819	The spec is organised by what the product *does*, never by how the code is
820	arranged. "Shared code" is not a requirement category: a rule both front-ends
821	follow is one feature, and its picture shows **both** the Now page and the
822	planner — a rule only half the site follows is not the feature. Those
823	cross-page features sit in their own part **after** the two page-by-page
824	segments, so each page reads as a whole first.
825	
826	Cross-page proof is ordinary: a case may navigate between the pages (or open a
827	second page, when something fixed at context creation — a device timezone —
828	has to differ) and stitch or animate the surfaces into one golden.
829	
830	### Prefer several pictures over one coded leaf
831	
832	Before routing a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`, ask whether it **decomposes
833	into observable states**. A statement joined by "and" usually does, and each
834	part is then its own numbered sub-leaf with its own picture — the parent
835	becomes a heading. The time wheel went this way: "5-minute steps, opens at
836	now + 2 h, ends at 29:55" was one coded leaf and is now `3.7.1`–`3.7.3`, three
837	crops anyone can check by eye. Sub-leaves are cheap; a coded assertion the
838	owner has to read code to trust is not.
839	
840	Reserve the coded kinds for what genuinely has no picture:
841	
842	- **`behavior`** — a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes
843	  downloaded, storage written), or a fact the OS paints rather than the page
844	  (a native `title` tooltip, a cursor — neither can appear in a screenshot).
845	- **`logic`** — a pure rule with no rendered surface at all. When the rule is
846	  about *how values are written*, prefer a **table** over prose: a case may
847	  declare `table: { columns, rows }`, the gallery renders it into the spec, and
848	  its `verify()` proves every row against the shipped code — so the table a
849	  reader sees is generated evidence, not a hand-typed claim.
850	
851	When a leaf lands in a coded kind *because* the product makes it invisible,
852	say so in its Notes and name what product change would make it visual — that
853	is a real finding about the UI, not just a testing limitation.
854	
855	### The browser is part of the expected
856	
857	- A golden is only comparable under the **exact Chromium that rendered it**.
858	  The harness pins the Playwright version and refuses any other
859	  (`shared/harness/browser.js`); CI installs that pin per run, the Claude
860	  sandbox ships it globally. **Bumping the pin re-renders every golden** — it
861	  is a re-baselining, done deliberately and approved like one, never a drive-by
862	  upgrade.
863	- When the comparison ever flaps, the fix is **more determinism, not a
864	  tolerance**: the comparator stays at zero diff. The determinism levers are
865	  all in one place (the harness): fixed clock via `page.clock`, fixed
866	  geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network, frozen
867	  animations, `--font-render-hinting=none --force-color-profile=srgb`.
868	
869	### Traps this harness already paid for (don't re-derive)
870	
871	- **Geolocation exists only on secure origins.** The fake origin is `https://`
872	  — route interception fulfils before any TLS, so no certificate is involved.
873	  On plain http the app silently keeps its built-in simulated clock and the
874	  whole render lands on the wrong day.
875	- **The app adopts the device clock only on an in-UK geolocation fix** — the
876	  harness's fixed location is central Edinburgh precisely so the pinned clock
877	  is what renders; deny geolocation (or move abroad) and you are rendering the
878	  app's own pre-set simulated moment instead, a different day file entirely.
879	- **A CSS freeze does not stop Web-Animations-API animations.** The planner's
880	  FLIP board diff runs through `element.animate` — the harness stubs it to
881	  land on end states; without the stub, captures race the animation.
882	- **Fonts arrive via the Google Fonts CSS URL**, so the vendored `fonts.css`'s
883	  `url(/__vendor/…)` references resolve against `fonts.googleapis.com` — the
884	  vendor route must match on path, host-agnostic, or every glyph silently
885	  falls back and all text shifts by a pixel.
886	- **Vendoring the web fonts is only half the font problem.** Every character
887	  they don't carry — an emoji, `▾`, `≤`, a Cyrillic show title — is drawn from
888	  the fonts *installed on the machine*, so the goldens quietly become a record
889	  of the renderer's font set. It cost a red CI lane: the walk-time line
890	  (`🚶 5 min · £16`) measured wider on the GitHub runner, wrapped, and every
891	  show card came out 21px taller. The harness now launches Chromium under a
892	  generated `FONTCONFIG_FILE` whose only font directory is
893	  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` — the host's fonts cannot reach the page. A new
894	  emoji or script in the product or the fixtures needs that subset rebuilt
895	  (see the folder's README), or it renders as tofu.
896	- **Reproducing a golden-flake locally: use the harness's own pixel comparator
897	  (`compare.js`), not a raw byte/hash compare.** On 2026-08-11 (#335) a first
898	  repro script hashed the rendered PNG's bytes across repeated cold renders
899	  and found a hash difference — looked like a reproduction of the flake, but
900	  `compare.js` (pixelmatch, zero tolerated diff) passed the identical images
901	  at 0 pixels differing. A byte-hash compare is strictly tighter than what CI
902	  actually enforces (bit-exact *pixels*, not encoder bytes), so it manufactures
903	  false positives; the real comparator is what settles whether a flake is real.
904	- **A red CI lane's diff image is unreachable from a session — reproduce it
905	  locally.** `ui-requirements` uploads a `requirements-failure-artifacts`
906	  artifact, but `download_workflow_run_artifact` hands back a
907	  `*.blob.core.windows.net` URL and the egress proxy denies it at CONNECT
908	  (`curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`). On 2026-08-11 a session
909	  burned the download and then came back ~4.5 minutes later to re-probe the
910	  proxy for the same image; the golden it was chasing ended the session
911	  undiagnosed. Use `get_job_logs` with a large `tail_lines` to learn *which*
912	  case failed, then re-run that case locally — `npm run test:ui` writes the
913	  `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/` itself.
914	- **A floating popup dies under a full-page screenshot** (the capture scrolls,
915	  and scroll dismisses tips/legends/optimizer pops). A popup-state case sets
916	  `viewportOnly: true` and captures the viewport crop.
917	- **"Ready" is not `networkidle`.** The pages settle their async work into
918	  observable state — the footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's
919	  show count. Wait on those (`case-helpers.js`), plus `document.fonts.ready`.
920	- **Hover-driven UI must be opened inside `capture()`, not `drive()`.** The
921	  runner settles the scroll between the two, and scrolling moves an element out
922	  from under the pointer — which fires `mouseleave` and closes anything the
923	  hover opened. That is correct product behaviour; the capture just has to
924	  happen on the right side of it.
925	
926	### The fixture freeze
927	
928	- `shared/fixtures/data/` is a snapshot of the **real committed data**, cast by
929	  the committed builder for state variety (sold-out / free / price-unknown /
930	  tight / every planner verdict). It is **frozen**: the nightly data refresh
931	  never touches it, and no case may reach for `data/` live files.
932	- Every deviation from the source bytes is documented as an `ADJUST` in the
933	  builder — a fixture edit without one is hand-invented data.
934	- Re-running the builder re-casts every golden. That is a re-baselining: run it
935	  only with the owner's approval, and land builder + fixtures + goldens +
936	  gallery in one reviewed change.
937	
938	### Golden approval, concretely
939	
940	- Surface the committed golden alongside `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png`
941	  and `.diff.png`, and ask the owner (AskUserQuestion popup, per-item, per the
942	  owner's preferences).
943	- Say so in the PR body — the goldens are the review surface.
944	- An intended UI change lands as: spec edit (doc-first, red) → implementation →
945	  `npm run refresh:ui` → the refreshed PNGs ride the same diff.
946
