input.title: Claudinite growth: rule revalidation
input.head: claudinite/claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation/2026-09-13-y2vb95
input.body:
Weekly `claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation` pass over this repo's local pack (scope: `.claudinite-settings.json`'s `claudinite-growth.pack_paths`, unset here, so the default `.claudinite/local/packs` → `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/`).

Re-probed every claim in `RULES.md` (and its `references.md`) whose truth lives outside this repo — the Claude harness's own tool contracts, GitHub/MCP tool behaviour, and this session's egress policy — and corrected what no longer held. Read-only probes only; nothing was merged, deleted, or notified as part of probing.

## Corrected (stale → fixed in this diff)

1. **Egress "Observed so far"** (`## Reaching the network`) — the 2026-09-04 "general egress open" observation is no longer current. Probed 2026-09-13 with `curl` against 8 hosts plus `$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status`: `fringeplan.com`, `maze.co`, `www.lyssna.com`, `unpkg.com`, `example.com`, `edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` all got `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`, confirmed as **policy** denials (not origin) via the proxy's own `recentRelayFailures` log; only `www.edfringe.com` (200) and `fonts.googleapis.com` (404, i.e. tunnel succeeded) got through. Added as a third data point — the policy visibly swings both ways within days, which is exactly why the rule's own directive ("probe it in this session first") stands unchanged.
2. **`edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` reachability** (data-pipeline section) — same probe reproduced a CONNECT-level policy denial today, reverting from the 2026-09-04 "server-side 403" (tunnel succeeded, origin refused) back to the 2026-08 "denied at CONNECT" shape. Added as a third dated data point.
3. **`actions_list`/`list_workflow_runs` per_page claim** — old text: "lowering `per_page` does not fix it" (evidenced by identical overflow at 25/10/3/2/1). Retested live: `list_workflow_runs` with no `perPage` overflowed at ~59K chars; with `perPage: 3` and again `perPage: 1` it returned cleanly, no truncation. The MCP tool's handling of `perPage` has evidently been fixed since that finding — corrected the rule to "pass `perPage` explicitly" rather than "don't bother lowering it."
4. **`list_pull_requests` merged-field claim** — old text: "`merged_at` is never populated, `fields` or not." Retested against three real closed-and-merged PRs (#682, #676, #670), with and without a `fields` filter: `merged` still always decodes `false`, but `merged_at` **is** populated in every case (cross-checked against `pull_request_read get` on PR #385, `merged: true`, as ground truth). Corrected the rule to use `merged_at` as the landed-ness signal instead of grepping `origin/main`'s commit subjects.
5. **`pull_request_read method=get_files` overflow claim** — old text: "treat it as skip the diff, not something to retry." Retested PR #207 (46 files, the PR named in the original claim): `perPage: 100` still hard-overflows exactly as before, but `perPage: 10` returned successfully (large, but under the limit). Corrected from "don't retry" to "retry at a smaller `perPage`."
6. **`download_workflow_run_artifact` tool-shape claim** — `ToolSearch` with `select:mcp__github__download_workflow_run_artifact` returns "No matching deferred tools found"; a keyword search shows it is now a `method` value on `mcp__github__actions_get` (`resource_id` = artifact ID), not a standalone tool. Corrected the invocation shape in the rule; the substance (the returned URL is an off-allowlist blob-storage host the proxy denies at CONNECT) is unchanged and not itself re-probed today.

## Holds (reconfirmed, no change)

- **`gh` CLI is not installed** — `which gh` → exit 1, no output.
- **The harness blocks a bare `sleep N`** — read directly off the current Bash tool's own contract text ("Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked... use Monitor with an until-loop"), the most authoritative and current source available.
- **Playwright/Chromium pre-install, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, the `chromium` symlink, and the `index.mjs` import with no `executablePath`** — `echo`'d the env var, `ls`/`readlink`'d the symlink chain, and ran a live `node -e` importing `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs` and launching Chromium (`chromium.launch()` succeeded, version 141.0.7390.37).
- **`search_issues`/`list_pull_requests`/`pull_request_read` shrink with `fields`/`minimal_output`** — consistent with this run's own `fields`-narrowed `list_pull_requests` calls, each a small payload.
- **RULES-1** (Chromium can't tunnel the proxy to an arbitrary host; route via `page.route` + `curl`) — not a retirement candidate: today's probe shows egress is if anything *more* restricted than when this was written, so the condition that would retire it ("the proxy lets headless Chromium tunnel directly") plainly doesn't hold.
- **RULES-4's directive** (fetch first, fall back to `WebSearch` only after a real failure, never a standing ban) — reinforced rather than retired: `fringeplan.com` itself flipped from reachable (2026-09-04) back to policy-denied (2026-09-13) inside this same file's evidence trail, which is exactly the "probe every time, don't trust the last verdict" case the rule already argues for.

## Doc-verified (owner decision, not a live probe)

- **RULES-5** (graphics-first, minimal-text wizard mockups per the owner's rejection of a buttons-and-prose first draft) — checked this repo's own record (recent design-concepts/trip-planner work) for any reversal; found none, decision stands as recorded.

## Unprobed (not disproven — named per the task's own rule)

- **RULES-2** (a subagent killed mid-run by a session rate limit hands back no report). Retirement would require actually inducing a rate-limit kill, which isn't a safe, deterministic, read-only probe and risks real work loss — left exactly as it stands.
- **`subscribe_pr_activity` denied mid-session when driving a PR to green** — the only way to test whether the owner would deny it now is to invoke it while actually driving a PR, which is the exact scenario the rule is about; not safely re-probable without deliberately courting the denial.
- **"Never `npm i playwright` into the scratchpad"** — re-running `npm i playwright` to check today's version-mismatch behaviour is a write action (fetches packages, touches `node_modules`/lockfiles), excluded by the read-only-probe rule; left unchanged.

## Not reached (budget)

- The requirements-harness section's web-platform claims (geolocation requires a secure origin, a CSS freeze doesn't stop Web-Animations-API animations, the Playwright-pin/golden-rebaseline claims) — stable, foundational specs judged lower risk of drift than the MCP/tool-contract claims above, and this run's remaining budget went to the higher-value corrections above instead.

`bash scripts/verify.sh` is green on this branch (0 blocking, 4 pre-existing advisories unrelated to this change).

This PR's diff sits entirely `under:.claudinite/local/packs`, which `task.json`'s `automerge` authorizes; `merge-policy.mjs --base main --policy 'under:.claudinite/local/packs'` returned `AUTOMERGE: yes`, so the branch's commit carries the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy` arming trailer.

Refs #687

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
